# Arbitrary-dimensional polytopal boundary midpoint repair

This extends the planar rebuilding theorem in
`candidate 229cbb48c7fa3080`
to polytopal fibers in every continuous dimension. It uses the audited
convex-surplus density-selection theorem, not a multivariate comonotone
maximality assertion. It also identifies the precise new elementary cap
payment and an exact obstruction to promoting it to source-cap order.

## 1. Data and conclusion

Let d>=1 and let K_-, K_0, K_+ be full-dimensional compact convex polytopes
in R^d satisfying

    (K_-+K_+)/2 subset K_0.                         (1)

Place them at integer bases -1,0,1. Let eta_z be their surface measures
on the normal bundle (n,z,X), with almost-everywhere outward normal n;
in d=1 this is counting measure on the two endpoints and their normals.
Set eta=sum_z eta_z. Let theta be an actual ambient cap law with fixed
physical trace selectors s_H, including any fixed supporting allocations,
and let

    W=int s_H dtheta(H),     nu=(W/beta)eta,     0<beta<1.

Suppose an actual normal-preserving physical martingale Pi transports
nu to eta. Thus its conditional target probabilities P_s satisfy

    int (z_t,X_t) P_s(dt)=(z_s,X_s),
    n_t=n_s almost surely.

Let gamma_- and gamma_+ be its physical endpoint target crossflows from
base-zero sources. Their equal normal marginal is tau. Then there exists
a replacement martingale Pi_new with the SAME source nu, target eta, and
physical crossflows gamma_-,gamma_+, and one conditional endpoint pairing
whose midpoint law rho satisfies

    rho<=eta_0.                                    (2)

The endpoint-source rows may be kept unchanged. Neither theta nor W nor
any cap allocation is changed. The middle-source rows generally change.
For the SAME selected pairing and every closed ambient halfspace H,

    gamma_-(H)+gamma_+(H)>=rho(H_0),                (3)

where H_0 is the trace on the middle fiber. This includes oblique H and
positive boundary mass; (3) uses literal closed indicators.

## 2. Original crossflow and its midpoint law

An endpoint source cannot change its base in a martingale supported at
-1,0,1. At a middle source s, the probabilities of the two endpoint
branches are therefore equal, say q(s). Pair these endpoint branches by
their conditional independent product, or any fixed measurable coupling.
The resulting endpoint tuple measure has mass int q dnu_0 and marginals
gamma_- and gamma_+. Denote its midpoint law by rho_old.

At a source with normal n, taking the scalar product of its continuous
barycenter equation with n yields

    q(s)[2h_0(n)-h_-(n)-h_+(n)]=0.                 (4)

Thus positive crossflow occurs only at a tight midpoint support relation.
All paired midpoints then lie on the actual middle support face, by (1)
and (4). Replacing each paired endpoint branch by twice its midpoint gives
an actual normal-preserving martingale

    nu_0 -> eta_0+2rho_old.                         (5)

The middle target marginal in the old martingale is exactly eta_0,
because endpoint sources cannot target base zero. This explains the full
eta_0 term in (5); it is not a residual submeasure.

## 3. Repair at a polytopal facet normal, d>=2

Fix n with m_n=tau({n})>0. The two endpoint surface measures at this normal
are nonzero, so their support faces F_-(n),F_+(n) are facets. Equation (4)
and (1) imply that their Minkowski average lies in F_0(n). This average
has positive (d-1)-dimensional measure, so F_0(n) is also a facet.

Use the common Euclidean tangent space n-perp and write every face point
as h_z(n)n+t. The two endpoint crossflow measures in t coordinates have
equal mass m_n and satisfy

    gamma_(minus,n)<=Leb_(d-1),
    gamma_(plus,n)<=Leb_(d-1).

Apply the audited density-selection theorem in tangent dimension d-1 to
the OLD endpoint tuple coupling at this normal. It gives another tuple
coupling Xi_n of these SAME physical marginals, whose midpoint law rho_n
satisfies

    rho_old,n <=_cx rho_n,       rho_n<=Leb_(d-1).  (6)

The common normal height is restored after taking tangent midpoints.
Every selected tuple remains supported on the actual endpoint facets,
so (1) and (4) put its midpoint in F_0(n). Consequently (6) is exactly

    rho_n<=eta_(0,n).                              (7)

Here convex order tests the whole physical middle face: restricting an
ambient convex function to this affine face gives a convex tangent test.
No lattice coordinate or normal is transformed.

Combining (5) and (6) gives

    nu_(0,n) <=_cx eta_(0,n)+2rho_n.                (8)

These are equal-mass compact measures. The compact martingale existence
theorem for convex order supplies a transport from the left side to the
right side, preserving the continuous barycenter. The normal and base
coordinates at this stage are fixed. This is the same martingale theorem
already proved and used in Section 5 of the planar source note; no new
selection or attainment assumption is added.

## 4. Rebuilding the entire middle transport

Disintegrate Xi_n over its midpoint z to obtain a conditional endpoint
tuple law Xi_(n,z). Let sigma_n=eta_(0,n)+2rho_n and define

    a_n=d eta_(0,n)/d sigma_n,
    b_n=d(2rho_n)/d sigma_n,
    a_n+b_n=1.

After the martingale in (8) arrives at its intermediate point z, retain
base zero and that point with probability a_n(z). With probability
b_n(z), draw an endpoint pair from Xi_(n,z) and choose either endpoint
with probability one half. The physical mean of this last pair equals
the intermediate point, including its base and normal height. Composition
is therefore a martingale from the ORIGINAL middle source.

Its target marginals are exactly

    eta_(0,n), gamma_(minus,n), gamma_(plus,n).

Indeed the endpoint branch has intermediate marginal 2rho_n, and each
of its two choices divides this by two. Its pair marginal is Xi_n.
Equivalently, half of that branch defines a tuple measure with midpoint
law rho_n and equal conditional endpoint branch masses at every source.
Thus it is also a genuine conditional endpoint pairing for the rebuilt
martingale, not merely an unrelated globally chosen endpoint coupling.

Keep all old endpoint-source rows. Their target marginals are exactly
eta_--gamma_- and eta_+-gamma_+, so the complete new target is eta. There
are finitely many polytopal facet normals. Apply this construction at each
with m_n>0 and retain the old rows at all others. The finite union of the
new Borel kernels is measurable. Summing (7) proves (2).

## 5. Continuous dimension one

For intervals K_z, the two possible normals are n=+1 and n=-1, and each
support face is a singleton of surface mass one. At a tight support
relation its endpoint pair has the unique midpoint equal to the middle
support point. Since gamma_(minus,n)<=eta_(minus,n), its mass m_n is at
most one. Thus rho_old,n=m_n delta_(middle endpoint)<=eta_(0,n).
No zero-dimensional density theorem is invoked. The old martingale and
its original pairing already satisfy (2).

The statement concerns boundary transport for d>=1. It makes no claim
about a surface-measure construction for OC's continuous dimension d=0.

## 6. Literal caps and fixed selectors

For every paired endpoint tuple and every affine functional ell,

    ell(0,(X_-+X_+)/2)
      =[ell(-1,X_-)+ell(1,X_+)]/2.

If the midpoint belongs to the closed halfspace {ell>=c}, at least one
endpoint belongs to it. This proves (3) pointwise and hence simultaneously
for all closed halfspaces using the one selected tuple law. It does not
depend on a zero-boundary-mass convention.

If H is proper on a full-dimensional polytopal fiber K_z, its boundary
plane has eta_z-measure zero. In d>=2, the plane cannot equal any facet
plane (that would make it supporting), so its intersection with every
facet has dimension at most d-2. In d=1 its boundary lies strictly inside
the interval and has no endpoint counting mass. Therefore

    gamma_-(partial H)=gamma_+(partial H)=rho(partial H_0)=0

whenever H is proper on all three fibers. On these measures the existing
trace selectors coincide almost everywhere with literal indicators, and
(3) becomes the fixed-selector inequality

    integral s_H dgamma_- + integral s_H dgamma_+
        >= integral s_H drho.                     (9)

The same conclusion holds if a given fiber is strictly full or empty,
with its boundary plane separated from that fiber. A cap may mix these
statuses among the three fibers. In general, the exact sufficient
condition is that the actual selectors equal the literal indicators
almost everywhere on the respective gamma_-,gamma_+,rho.

At a positive-area supporting coincidence that condition need not hold:
the prescribed supporting allocation is additional data. The construction
preserves that allocation but does not establish a new relation among
such allocations. Thus (3) remains valid there, whereas (9) requires the
stated selector condition.

## 7. A genuine but limited capacity payment

For each repaired normal n and every closed ambient H, (2) and the fixed
mass m_n imply

    rho_n(H_0)
       =m_n-rho_n(F_0(n) outside H_0)
       >=[m_n-eta_(0,n)(F_0(n) outside H_0)]_+.

Apply the pointwise cap inequality at this normal and sum. The result is

    gamma_-(H)+gamma_+(H)
      >= sum_n [m_n-eta_(0,n)(F_0(n) outside H_0)]_+.                 (10)

This is additional numerical cap information supplied by density repair.
It is strongest when the middle trace captures almost an entire facet.
The complement is strict because H is closed; no boundary term has been
silently dropped. The same inequality for allocations follows under the
selector condition of Section 6.

The elementary bound is sharp using only a mass m_n and domination by
eta_(0,n): put as much of rho_n as possible in the complement and put the
remaining mass in H_0. Identical endpoint facets with diagonal endpoint
pairing realize arbitrary such subdensities as geometric midpoint laws.
This sharpness assertion concerns these local density-and-mass data; it
does not assert that every such law comes from a critical OC cap law.

## 8. Exact obstruction to source-cap conversion after repair

Even with an actual cap law, a rebuilt whole physical martingale, and
rho<=eta_0, it is false in general that

    nu_0(H_0)<=eta_0(H_0)+gamma_-(H)+gamma_+(H).     (11)

Use the exact square construction in Section 4 of the planar source note:
K_-=K_0=K_+=[-1,1]^2, beta=19/36, with the eight equally weighted actual
caps

    {a z+v.X>=-1/3},
    v in {e_1,-e_1,e_2,-e_2}, a in {-2,2}.

On each middle edge, parametrized by tangent t in [-1,1],

    dnu_0/dt=18/19+(9/19)1_{|t|<1/3}.

The source note gives an explicit rebuilt martingale with

    gamma_-=gamma_+=(1/19)eta_0,
    rho=(1/19)eta_0.

For completeness, on each edge transport nu_0 to (21/19)dt by retaining
the common density and sending the central excess 6/19 equally to t-2/3
and t+2/3. Given that intermediate point, choose target base zero with
probability 19/21 and each endpoint base with probability 1/21. The
endpoint tangent points are equal, so diagonal pairing gives the stated
rho. Retain the endpoint sources' old identity rows of density 18/19.
All original source and target marginals are correct.

Take the closed cap H={X_2<=1/4}, proper on all three square fibers. The
middle surface measure captured is 9/2: the bottom edge contributes 2
and the two vertical edges contribute 5/4 each. On each vertical edge
the source capture is

    (18/19)(5/4)+(9/19)(7/12)=111/76.

The full bottom edge contributes 42/19. Hence

    nu_0(H_0)=195/38,
    eta_0(H_0)+gamma_-(H)+gamma_+(H)
       =(21/19)(9/2)=189/38.

Thus (11) fails by exactly 3/19. Every relevant selector is an ordinary
proper trace and has zero boundary mass. The midpoint density repair does
not fix this failure: its purpose is to give a more spread midpoint law
in convex order, and halfspace capture is not ordered by that relation.

This example is not a critical OC cap law: its individual volume fractions
do not equal beta. It therefore rules out an automatic consequence of the
stated boundary-martingale data, not an argument using additional critical
volume constraints. It is not an OC counterexample.

## 9. Why arbitrary higher-dimensional convex bodies need more work

For a general convex body in d>=3, positive-dimensional nonfacet support
faces can occur over an uncountable set of normals carrying surface-area
measure. Their conditional surface laws need not be uniform relative to
the intrinsic measure of those faces. Consequently the polytopal proof
does not extend merely by replacing its finite normal sum by an integral.

For an explicit geometric example in d=3, let

    K={(x,y,z):0<=z<=1, sqrt(x^2+y^2)<=z}.

Its lateral surface is parametrized by

    (theta,r) -> (r cos theta,r sin theta,r),   0<=r<=1,

with surface element sqrt(2) r dr dtheta and normal
n(theta)=(cos theta,sin theta,-1)/sqrt(2). Each such support face is the
generator segment indexed by theta. Relative to its normal marginal
(sqrt(2)/2)dtheta, the conditional surface measure is the probability
law 2r dr. This is not uniform on the segment; its density relative to
arc length is sqrt(2)r.

The bounded-Lebesgue-density selection theorem does not by itself turn
endpoint laws bounded by these nonconstant conditional measures into a
midpoint law bounded by the middle conditional measure. The cone example
demonstrates the missing uniformity, not the falsity of a possible weighted
replacement theorem. Such a theorem, or a rigorous compatible limiting
argument, would be additional work. Neither is asserted here.

The full OC conversion remains open within this proof route: the repaired
transport and payment (10) do not supply a parity budget, a center, or the
factor gamma_d. Equation (11) shows why source-cap order cannot be inserted
as an automatic final step.
